tools.name: search_templates
tools.description: Search the Meme Studio catalog by name, keywords or what the meme is used for (intent), in Spanish or English. Best matches first, each with what it is used for and whether it is animated: an animated template gives an animated GIF.

tools.name: suggest_templates
tools.description: The best first step: give the joke or the situation, in Spanish or English, and get the templates that fit it best (five by default), each with what it is used for, whether it is animated and its slots: what goes in each one (hint) and about how many characters fit (fits_chars). tools.name: popular_templates
tools.description: Templates people choose most in Meme Studio (trending this week or most used overall) or, with kind new, the latest added to the catalog.

tools.name: create_meme
tools.description: Create a meme on exactly one of: template (a catalog id), image (your own picture in base64 or a data: URL; JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, up to 5 MB and 25 megapixels (16 for WebP, 8 for GIF, less for a large progressive JPEG), 100 px or more a side, at most 4:1; a GIF gives its first frame) or image_url

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_meme · Private data: create_meme · Public sink: create_meme.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_meme · Private data: create_meme · Public sink: create_meme

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_templates" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
